article_title: Moving toward Instructional Coherence: How Four Popular Student-Centered Approaches Deepen Identity, Agency, Equity, and Community
citation: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Instructional coherence framework: four student-centered approaches share commitments to identity, agency, equity, and community
description: The paper offers a framework for understanding formative assessment, deeper learning, culturally responsive and sustaining education, and personalized learning as complementary rather than competing approaches. It states that the four approaches 'share a common aspirational commitment—to provide student learning experiences rooted in developing identity, prioritizing learner agency, educating for equity, and honoring and activating community assets.' The framework is intended to help school leaders build an instructional vision using practices shared across all four approaches, since no single approach alone provides the structures to achieve that aspiration.
requirements: School communities introducing or integrating multiple student-centered learning practices must honor the capacities and strengths of each approach
constraints: The resource is not exhaustive of all student-centered learning approaches; it focuses on these four at the secondary level
target_learners: K-12 students, particularly secondary school students
target_learning_goals: Self-directed learning
learner agency
student engagement
equity-centered instruction
examples: The paper provides a figure summarizing key elements of each of the four instructional approaches for school leaders
key_sources: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED655925

article_title: Moving toward Instructional Coherence: How Four Popular Student-Centered Approaches Deepen Identity, Agency, Equity, and Community
citation: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Formative assessment as eliciting, interpreting, and using evidence of learning during learning to build metacognition and self-regulation
description: The paper defines formative assessment using Bell and Cowie's definition as 'the process used by teachers and students to notice, recognize, and respond to student learning in order to enhance that learning, during the learning.' It prioritizes learning how to learn and metacognition: teachers explicitly teach students to elicit, interpret, and use evidence of learning during instruction, gradually shifting power to students who learn to self-monitor independently and with peers. Daily routines such as student discourse, peer feedback, and self-assessment, supported by shared success criteria, are the operational core.
requirements: Teachers explicitly teach daily routines and practices such as student discourse, peer feedback, and self-assessment
Teachers and students share a conception of what learning will look like through the use of success criteria
constraints: Requires teachers to move away from a traditional teacher-directed instructional model
target_learners: K-12 students, particularly secondary school students
target_learning_goals: Metacognition
self-regulation of learning
use of evidence of learning to guide next steps
examples: Students can say 'This is where I am in my learning, this is how I know, and these are next steps I can take' as evidence of self-regulation
key_sources: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED655925

article_title: Moving toward Instructional Coherence: How Four Popular Student-Centered Approaches Deepen Identity, Agency, Equity, and Community
citation: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Deeper learning as real-world, transferable competency development across academic content, critical thinking, collaboration, self-direction, and mindsets
description: The paper describes deeper learning as a broad term for learning experiences building the skills, dispositions, and knowledge students need for 21st century jobs and civic life. It states that 'Compelling, real-world content and skills in deeper learning tasks enable transferability and application of knowledge across contexts (Honig & Rainey, 2015).' It lists five core competencies attributed to the Hewlett Foundation: mastering academic content, critical thinking and problem-solving, collaboration and communication, self-directed learning, and adaptive academic mindsets. Instructional strategies include interdisciplinary projects, work-based learning, and project-based learning.
requirements: Clear goals and expectations for what students should know and be able to do
Challenges connected to real-life tasks that students work on collaboratively
constraints: Opportunities for students to demonstrate their learning are typically summative in nature
target_learners: Secondary school students
target_learning_goals: Critical thinking and problem-solving
collaboration and communication
transfer of knowledge across contexts
self-directed learning
examples: Student-led conferences, portfolios, capstone projects, advisories, and employer-based mentorship assessments are common in deeper learning settings
key_sources: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED655925

article_title: Moving toward Instructional Coherence: How Four Popular Student-Centered Approaches Deepen Identity, Agency, Equity, and Community
citation: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Culturally responsive and sustaining education as asset-based use of student cultural identities in learning and curriculum codesign
description: The paper presents CRSE as an approach advancing educational equity by creating culturally affirming and inclusive learning environments. It states that 'Culturally responsive pedagogy uses diverse cultural knowledge, experiences, frames of reference, and methods of expression to make learning engaging, relevant, and effective for students from a range of cultural backgrounds (Gay, 2010).' Culturally sustaining practice additionally sustains evolving student cultures and has the explicit goal of supporting multilingualism and multiculturalism. Students and communities act as codesigners of curriculum, and students are empowered as agents of social change.
requirements: An important condition for CRSE is to allow for reshaping the curriculum or delivery of services by including students as codesigners of curriculum
Educators value all racial, linguistic, and cultural identities and use them as vehicles of learning
constraints: CRSE supports cultural pluralism, not cultural assimilation
target_learners: K-12 students from a range of cultural backgrounds, including historically marginalized students
target_learning_goals: Positive racial, ethnic, and cultural identity development
recognizing and critiquing social inequalities
academic achievement alongside intellectual and political empowerment
examples: Active teaching methods such as student-controlled discourse and small-group instruction help students connect across lines of difference
key_sources: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED655925

article_title: Moving toward Instructional Coherence: How Four Popular Student-Centered Approaches Deepen Identity, Agency, Equity, and Community
citation: Browning, A., Kaminsky, C., & Gerzon, N. (2022). Moving toward instructional coherence: How four popular student-centered approaches deepen identity, agency, equity, and community. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: Personalized learning as learner-centered variation of place, pace, content, and strategies guided by ongoing evidence
description: The paper defines personalized learning as 'a philosophy or broad orientation to learning that places the individual learner at the center of the learning process so that resources, strategies, and content are varied to meet the individual's learning needs and preferences.' Teachers act in a facilitative role, using multiple sources of data, learning progressions, and success criteria to scaffold learning opportunities. The approach prioritizes student voice and choice and adaptive teaching, and it is explicitly technology agnostic—blended and digital learning are common strategies but not required.
requirements: Teachers rely on multiple sources of data and information to understand individual and group learning progress
Teachers scaffold learning opportunities to guide and prompt students to progress
constraints: Personalized learning is technology agnostic and does not require or rely on digital resources or instruction
target_learners: K-12 students, particularly secondary school students
target_learning_goals: Active engagement
academic success
student motivation
preparation for postsecondary opportunities
examples: Place, pace, content, and strategies may vary depending on student learning goals and needs

article_title: The Impact of NBA Math Hoops on Students' Math Achievement: A Randomized Controlled Trial
citation: McKinney, D., Walters, K., Powell, K., Sabalburo, E., & Morton, C. (2026). The impact of NBA Math Hoops on students' math achievement: A randomized controlled trial. WestEd. https://www.wested.org
title: NBA Math Hoops
description: NBA Math Hoops is a STEM learning program developed by Learn Fresh in partnership with the NBA and WNBA, built around an interactive board game using real player statistics. "As they play an interactive board game and complete associated lessons built around real NBA and WNBA player statistics, students have opportunities to build fluency in arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percentages, and data analysis." The program includes 10 supporting lessons and has reached over 1.4 million students across all 50 states since 2012.
requirements: Requires teacher training (2-3 hours) covering game rules, lesson review, and implementation planning
Requires board game materials, player cards, and 10-sided dice
Requires 90-minute instructional blocks
constraints: Materials and shipping costs are covered by Learn Fresh for participating programs
target_learners: Rising 4th, 5th, and 6th grade students
Students in underresourced communities
target_learning_goals: Math fluency in arithmetic, fractions, decimals, percentages
Data analysis and probability
Critical thinking and problem-solving
Collaboration and sportsmanship
examples: In the RCT, students played the board game in pairs, computing sums, differences, products, and quotients of two 10-sided dice rolls to select shot locations and player cards with real shooting statistics
key_sources: McKinney, D., Walters, K., Powell, K., Sabalburo, E., & Morton, C. (2026). The impact of NBA Math Hoops on students' math achievement: A randomized controlled trial. WestEd. https://eric.ed.gov/?id=ED681343
